title: 20 Years of European Credit on Tradeweb
summary: Twenty years after Tradeweb launched its electronic European credit marketplace, we reflect on how data, a broad liquidity network, flexible protocols and automation have extended the reach of trader expertise.
body_markdown:
#### *Twenty years after Tradeweb launched its electronic European credit marketplace, we reflect on how data, a broad liquidity network, flexible protocols and automation have extended the reach of trader expertise.*


Some have described the next chapter of[credit trading](https://www.tradeweb.com/our-markets/institutional/credit/) as the rise of the “super trader.” Whatever the label, the bigger story isn't about technology replacing the trader. It's about two decades of market evolution that have expanded the trader's toolkit, providing greater visibility, broader access to liquidity and more choice in how to execute.


When we brought electronic trading to European credit in June 2006, the market was fragmented and largely navigated through bilateral conversations, dealer runs and phone calls. What followed was a steady expansion of electronic trading’s role as the market weathered the global financial crisis, MiFID II, COVID-era volatility and geopolitical uncertainty. Twenty years on, what stands out is not one moment of transformation, but how quickly trading needs evolved and how the market responded.


####
Building Transparency: The RFQ Era


The first phase of electronic credit trading was about bringing greater visibility to an inherently opaque market.


Electronic request-for-quote (RFQ) transformed how participants interacted with the European credit market. Traders could replace sequential phone calls with a competitive, multi-dealer workflow, making best execution more transparent, consistent and demonstrable. That workflow remains a foundation of electronic trading, and the scale of that access


has grown from 21 dealers at launch to 60+ liquidity providers today.


A decade in, the conversation had already moved beyond simply replacing the phone call. Clients were increasingly focused on identifying the other side of the trade, transferring risk more effectively and navigating a market that had become larger, faster and more interconnected. Regulatory change accelerated that evolution: MiFID II, which took effect in January 2018, reinforced the value of electronic workflows through its emphasis on transparency, best execution and auditability.


#### Expanding Choice: From Price through Execution


The innovations that followed were shaped through ongoing collaboration between clients, dealers and Tradeweb. Many began with a practical question from the market: how could clients find relevant liquidity and move risk without unnecessarily exposing their intentions? How could they automate without losing control and uncover less visible opportunities? Our intent has never been to prescribe a single path to liquidity, but to give clients the choice and flexibility to respond to each market moment.


Dealer streams and axes evolved from liquidity signals into indicators embedded within execution workflows, helping traders assess where liquidity existed and which opportunities were most relevant. That supply became more visible, more contextual and increasingly actionable. Meanwhile, the growth of fixed income ETFs and passive investment strategies increased the need to rebalance portfolios efficiently.


[Portfolio trading (PT)](https://www.tradeweb.com/our-markets/institutional/credit/portfolio-trading/) marked a significant shift. Having already proven its value in the U.S., European Credit PT launched in November 2019, ten months after the U.S. Credit launch. For a market accustomed to trading bonds one at a time, the ability to execute an entire portfolio on a contingent basis transformed hundreds of individual trades into a single coordinated decision. In the first half of 2026, European credit PT volume on Tradeweb reached a record approximately €63 billion, up around 12% year-on-year, with Q1 and Q2 2026 representing the two strongest quarters recorded to date. ** In June 2026, we extended that capability with electronic spread trading for European credit portfolios, bringing a manual workflow onto the platform.


Automation evolved in parallel, moving from saving time and cost to managing execution through changing conditions. Rules-based workflows integrated with Order Management System (OMS) and Execution Management System (EMS) infrastructure made automation practical. Over time, the question shifted from “Should I automate?” to “How much can I automate?” as traders gained confidence refining their execution rules through volatility. The proportion of European corporate credit RFQ trades executed via[Tradeweb’s automated execution tool (AiEX)](https://www.tradeweb.com/our-markets/institutional/trade-cycle/automated-trading/) rose from 53% in 2020 to 82% in the first three quarters of 2026, ** illustrating how automation has become embedded within day-to-day credit trading workflows. **


As electronic trading volumes grew and balance sheet constraints tightened, dealers faced a different challenge: how to manage residual inventory and recycle risk more efficiently. New workflows emerged to connect institutional clients with sources of supply that had previously been harder to access electronically. Dealer Sweep extended access to residual wholesale liquidity, while SNAP IOI brought it directly into institutional workflows. This gave European Credit clients access to over €26 billion in nominal value across 8,000 - 9,000 ISINs they would not otherwise have accessed *.* It was another step in reducing fragmentation across previously separate pools of capital.


#### The When, Who and How of the Trade


The market's focus has expanded from sourcing liquidity to identifying the most relevant source for each trade and determining how best to engage it. Increasingly, the advantage lies not in having more information, but in synthesising it more effectively by connecting the right insight to the right execution decision at the right moment.


The questions now extend beyond “Where does liquidity lie?” to “When should I trade? Who should I trade with? How should I trade?”


Predictive pre-trade tools bring liquidity signals, market data and historical execution patterns together to help answer them. TARA, our AI-powered research assistant introduced in 2026, combines Tradeweb's proprietary data, liquidity insights and artificial intelligence to turn market information into actionable trading intelligence. Its value is not another screen of information, but relevant context that can inform dealer selection, likely outcomes and the most appropriate route to liquidity.


#### The Future We See


Looking back, the defining feature of European credit on Tradeweb has been neither a single innovation nor the shift to electronic trading alone. It has been the continual expansion of the credit trader's toolkit.


Transparency created choice. Connectivity expanded opportunity. Automation and intelligence are helping traders put both to work. European credit ADV on Tradeweb reached €1.6 billion in the first three quarters of 2026, exceeding the full-year 2025 average by 14%, reflecting the continued growth of electronic trading.


The trader remains at the centre. Technology can surface patterns, narrow the field and remove manual work. Human judgement determines when circumstances have changed, when a model should be challenged and how experience and relationships should shape the response. The next era belongs to traders who combine those strengths most effectively.


That is the making of a credit super trader: connecting information, liquidity and execution to make better decisions, faster.
